Medicare and Medicaid’s 60-year legacy isn’t about celebration—it’s about collapse. New York’s Medicaid system hemorrhages $55B annually in improper payments, duplicate programs, and ER misuse by non-citizens exploiting loopholes. Over 1.3 million New Yorkers face coverage loss not because of funding gaps, but because bureaucrats prioritize bloated contracts over patient care.

The real issue? Hospitals drowning in waste while illegal immigration strains resources meant for citizens. Taxpayer-funded care should protect veterans and working Americans, not subsidize systemic failure.

Until Albany slashes bureaucracy and enforces immigration laws, no amount of “fighting” will fix this disaster.

Hospitals in LA alone burn $3.7B annually in federal Medicaid funds while failing to meet translation mandates, then blame language barriers instead of their own waste. Meanwhile, Medicaid leaks $55B yearly in improper payments, duplicate programs, and ER misuse by non-citizens.

Prioritize veterans and taxpayers, not bureaucrats who can’t track their own spending. High-quality care starts with accountability, not blank checks for bloat.

Medicare’s collapse isn’t from reform—it’s from decades of Biden-era bureaucratic bloat, Medicaid fraud, and unchecked illegal immigration draining resources. The OBBB Act cuts $1T from programs riddled with waste, redirecting funds to Americans who paid into the system.

Real problem? 10M+ illegals abusing emergency mandates while hospitals inflate costs.

Fix the fraud, enforce the border, and watch care improve.

Higher costs? Absolutely. But the answer isn’t more federal spending—it’s cutting waste. The Child Care for Working Families Act (S. 1092) pumps billions into bureaucratic programs while failing to address systemic inefficiencies.

Meanwhile, the Big Beautiful Bill (H.R. 1) slashes $1.6T in bloat, redirecting funds to growth-first policies that actually lower costs for families. Democrats want to expand government control; Republicans are delivering fiscal discipline.

Real relief comes from empowering taxpayers, not inflating budgets.
